title: The Garden That Remembered Rain
synopsis: When a city loses its rain, two siblings follow the clues hidden in an extraordinary rooftop garden.

chapters.title: The Unexpected Message
paragraphs: The first sign was so small that most people would have mistaken it for a printing error. Nia, a curious eleven-year-old inventor had come to a crowded city where clouds have stopped arriving expecting routine work. Instead, Nia found a glass jar containing a single silver raindrop. The object was ordinary enough to fit in a pocket, yet it did not belong to the place or the hour. That contradiction would prove more important than the object itself.

Arun, her patient younger brother had a different interpretation. "A clue only tells us where to look," Arun said, "not what to believe." Nia wrote down the observation before answering. The people around them were eager for a quick conclusion, but a conclusion reached too early could make an innocent person carry the blame.

Mrs. Sol, the rooftop gardener pointed out a detail the others had missed. The detail connected the day's discovery to a decision that nobody had questioned for years. It was tempting to call the connection a coincidence. Instead, they compared dates, asked careful questions, and listened to the answers even when the answers complicated their plan.

Introduce the characters and the unusual clue that disturbs an ordinary day. Their investigation returned again to a glass jar containing a single silver raindrop. What had seemed like a single mystery was also a story about trust: who kept records, who was believed, and who had been left out. Nia realized that finding the truth would not be enough unless they considered what would happen after telling it.

As the day ended, Nia and Arun made a practical decision. They would preserve the evidence, speak to the people most affected, and resist the pressure to turn uncertainty into accusation.
